title.t: der blaue Pullover, den blauen Pullover
title.s: Adjective endings after der, die, das

grammar.explain:
After **sein**, an adjective has no ending: **Der Pullover ist blau.** But when the adjective stands **before a noun**, it needs an ending: **der blaue Pullover**. (English adjectives never change – German ones do.)
After the definite article **der, die, das** – and after **dieser, welcher, jeder** – there are only two endings: **-e** and **-en**.
**-e** in the **nominative singular** (**der blaue Pullover, die blaue Jacke, das blaue Kleid**) and in the **accusative singular** of feminine and neuter nouns (**die blaue Jacke, das blaue Kleid**).
**-en** everywhere else: the **accusative masculine** (**den blauen Pullover**), the whole **dative** (**dem blauen Pullover, der blauen Jacke**) and **all plurals** (**die blauen Schuhe**).
The table shows the nominative, accusative and dative.

title.t: billiger als, so teuer wie, am besten

grammar.explain:
To compare two things, add **-er** to the adjective and use **als** (*than*): **Die Jacke ist billiger als der Mantel.** German always uses **-er**, even with long adjectives – there is no word like *more*: **bequem → bequemer** (*more comfortable*). After a comparative, always use **als**, never wie.
Many short adjectives also get an **umlaut**: **alt → älter, groß → größer, jung → jünger, kurz → kürzer, lang → länger, warm → wärmer**. With **teuer** the e drops: **teurer**.
The **superlative** is **am …-sten**: **am billigsten, am bequemsten**. After **-d, -t, -s, -ß, -z** add **-esten**: **am ältesten, am kürzesten** (exception: **am größten**).
Some forms are irregular: **gut – besser – am besten, viel – mehr – am meisten, gern – lieber – am liebsten**.
To say two things are equal, use **so … wie** or **genauso … wie** (*as … as, just as … as*): **Der Rock ist so teuer wie die Hose.** **nicht so … wie** = *not as … as*.
Before a noun, comparatives and superlatives take the normal adjective endings: **der billigere Rock, das teuerste Kleid**.
